clue.text: About time — pull in abdomen desperately (one who's trying to look sexy?)

definitions.text: one who's trying to look sexy?

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go round the time abbreviation, so About signals one piece placed outside another
done desperately, the letters of pull in abdomen are thrown into wild disorder

explanation.surface: Someone sucks in their stomach in a desperate bid to look attractive, and it is about time too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desperately' rearranges PULL IN ABDOMEN, and 'About' wraps those letters around T for time.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman with very pale, silvery hair dyed for glamour is the classic image of a bombshell trying to look alluring.

clue.text: Do exercises in bad shape to begin with — they won't bring much joy

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: the exercises sit within the word for bad

parts.note: poor means bad
PE is physical education, school exercises

indicators.note: only the opening letter of shape is used

explanation.surface: Doing exercises when out of condition is no fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' is a noun here, a social event, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Party poopers are spoilsports who dampen everyone's fun at a gathering.

clue.text: Romance a special one? Not half!

indicators.note: only half of the manager's surname is kept, the second half dropped

parts.note: José Mourinho, the football manager, famously called himself the Special One

explanation.surface: Someone is asked whether a love affair is something special, and answers emphatically yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for 'very much so', but here it cuts MOURINHO to its first four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An amour is a love affair, a romance, especially a secret one.

clue.text: Naive and stupid, snorting cocaine earlier

indicators.note: snorting takes the drug in, so the rearranged letters hold it
stupid suggests the letters of naive and are jumbled senselessly

parts.note: C is slang shorthand for cocaine

explanation.surface: A naive person stupidly took cocaine some time before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stupid' rearranges NAIVE AND, and 'snorting' puts C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in advance means doing it beforehand, ahead of time.

clue.text: Aim to have day in American hills

indicators.note: the plan and day sit within the American letters

parts.note: US means American
an aim is a plan

explanation.surface: A walker plans a day out in the American hills.
explanation.definitionFit: Uplands are high ground, hilly country.

clue.text: Neither down about college failure

indicators.note: the both-up phrase goes round the college letter

parts.note: if neither is down, both are up

explanation.surface: Someone who failed to get into college finds both their options have fallen through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neither down' is a riddle: if neither is down, then both are up.
explanation.definitionFit: A botch-up is a bungled job, a mess or failure.

clue.text: Liberal entering has been received topless — he'd get an eyeful!

indicators.note: the Liberal letter goes into what remains
the first letter of the radio word is removed

parts.note: roger is the radio reply meaning a message has been received

explanation.surface: A Liberal enters a place where someone has been seen topless, a voyeur's delight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' cuts ROGER to OGER, and L goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogler stares lecherously, so he looks for a good eyeful.

clue.text: Assume it's a 'no' for replacement gifts

parts.note: to don clothes is to assume them

indicators.note: the letters of it's a no are put in new positions

explanation.surface: Someone assumes the answer is no and replaces the presents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for replacement' rearranges ITSANO into ATIONS.
explanation.definitionFit: Donations are gifts, especially to charity.

clue.text: Girl from Welsh valley extremely down about leaving

indicators.note: leaving says the turned pair departs from the valley's name

parts.note: the Rhondda is a famous valley in South Wales, once a coal-mining area

indicators.note: about turns the two end letters of down round the other way
only the end letters of down are taken

explanation.surface: A girl from the Welsh valleys is feeling really low about having to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' gives DN from 'down', 'about' turns it to ND, and 'leaving' takes those letters out of RHONDDA.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhoda is a woman's given name.

clue.text: Western director screens short story — never mind

indicators.note: the director's name hides the story within it

parts.note: Sergio Leone directed spaghetti Westerns

indicators.note: the last letter of the story word is dropped

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A director of Westerns shows a brief tale on screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' drops the last letter of the story word, and 'screens' hides it inside Sergio Leone's surname, as a screen conceals what is behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: Let alone is used like 'never mind' to say something is even less likely.

clue.text: Horny as hell, dropping spades — it maybe could lead to this

definitions.text: Horny as hell, dropping spades — it maybe could lead to this

indicators.note: maybe suggests a possible rearrangement of the letters
one letter for the card suit is let fall from horny as hell

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for spades in card games

explanation.surface: Feeling very randy and abandoning the gardening tools could lead to some fun in the barn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' takes S from HORNY AS HELL, IT is added and 'maybe' rearranges the lot. The whole clue also says where such lust may end.
explanation.definitionFit: A roll in the hay is a casual romp, the likely result of being very aroused.

clue.text: Wish to keep going round state capital

indicators.note: the wish word holds the other piece inside

parts.note: a yen is a longing or wish

indicators.note: the word for state is turned backwards

parts.note: to aver is to state

explanation.surface: A desire to keep travelling round a state capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' reverses the verb for state, and 'to keep' has the wish word hold it; 'state' looks like a country but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Yerevan is the capital city of Armenia.

clue.text: Theatrical friend in hotel, having forgotten new address

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: the letter for new is left out

parts.note: an oration is a formal address or speech

explanation.surface: An actor's friend in a hotel forgets the new address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having forgotten' takes N out of ORATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Horatio is Hamlet's loyal friend in Shakespeare's play, so a stage companion.

clue.text: Temper! Losing head a lot

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: to temper is to soften or moderate

explanation.surface: A warning about temper: losing your head happens a lot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Temper!' looks like a noun of anger but is the verb to moderate; 'Losing head' cuts SOFTEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Often means frequently, many times, a lot.

clue.text: Paper on strike cutting the supply

indicators.note: the two pieces cut into the rearranged letters
supply is read as in a supple manner, so the letters of the bend freely

parts.note: in cricket the on side is the leg side, so on gives LEG
to rap is to strike

explanation.surface: Newspaper workers on strike cut off the supply of papers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' is read as the adverb of supple, so it rearranges 'the'; 'cutting' puts the cricket word and the strike word inside. 'on' is the leg side in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: The Telegraph is a British daily newspaper.

clue.text: Big game reserve visited by a Member of Parliament?

indicators.note: the reserve word takes the other piece inside

parts.note: a sub is a substitute, a reserve player
per means a, as in so much a day
a parliament is the collective noun for owls, so one member of it is an owl

explanation.surface: A game reserve gets a visit from an MP.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the joke: a parliament of owls.
explanation.definitionFit: The Super Bowl is the championship game of American football, the biggest match of the season.

clue.text: Nudge when maintaining one's balance

indicators.note: the nudge word holds the letter for one

parts.note: a nudge is a reminder
one gives A, as in a or one

explanation.surface: A gentle nudge helps someone keep their balance.
explanation.definitionFit: The remainder is what is left over, the balance of an amount.

clue.text: Pound's poetry, one admitted, having a lot of charm, initially

indicators.note: the trimmed charm word comes first
most of the charm word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: pull is attraction or charm

indicators.note: the poetry word lets the one inside

parts.note: verse is poetry
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Ezra Pound's poetry, it is admitted, has a lot of charm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound's' reads as Pound is, the verb; 'Pound' looks like the poet Ezra Pound.
explanation.definitionFit: To pound something is to crush it, so pulverise is a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Helping one ingenue to conceal affair

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the naive word hides the affair word inside

parts.note: a naif is a naive person, an ingenue
a do is a social affair or party

explanation.surface: Someone helps an innocent young woman cover up an affair.
explanation.definitionFit: Collecting money in aid of a cause means for the benefit of it, helping it.

clue.text: Use up reserves of energy mating — stop! (both stripped)

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: the two words each lose their outer letters

explanation.surface: A couple exhaust their energy reserves making love and cry stop, both naked.
explanation.walkthrough: '(both stripped)' looks like a comment on the lovers but strips the ends from 'mating' and 'stop'.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat into savings is to consume part of them gradually.

clue.text: Occupying room as on-off lodger, might you say?

indicators.note: the answer occupies a run of letters inside room as on-off

explanation.surface: An on-off lodger occupies a room.
explanation.walkthrough: A Freemason belongs to a lodge, so in a playful sense he is a 'lodger'.
explanation.definitionFit: Masons meet in lodges, so the clue jokingly calls a lodge member a lodger.

clue.text: 'Excellent beer' in review for Crown and Sceptre?

indicators.note: reviewing looks back, so the letters are read in reverse order

parts.note: A1 means excellent, with the 1 read as the letter I
lager is a beer

explanation.surface: A pub called the Crown and Sceptre gets its beer praised in a review.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crown and Sceptre' sounds like a pub name, matching the beer; the question mark marks them as examples.
explanation.definitionFit: Regalia are royal emblems such as the crown and sceptre.

clue.text: Pub grub like this shouldn't be too fattening

definitions.text: grub like this shouldn't be too fattening
definitions.meaning: ..., short for low-calorie, describes food that is not fattening

explanation.surface: Pub food of this kind should not put on the pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: The local is a regular pub, and lo-cal food is low in calories.

clue.text: Victory? Sore loser back in touch is claiming one …

indicators.note: the loser's name takes the one inside

parts.note: Donald Trump is famous for refusing to accept defeat
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the last letter of touch is taken

explanation.surface: A bitter loser, back in contact, claims victory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back in' gives H, the end of 'touch'.
explanation.definitionFit: A triumph is a great victory.

clue.text: Mike's gone back in lead perhaps

parts.note: Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet, the 's read as has

indicators.note: the word for gone is read backwards

parts.note: late means dead, gone

explanation.surface: Mike has gone back to take the lead role.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead is an example of a metal, flagged by perhaps.

clue.text: … bloke's a show-off! Think he could be desperate

parts.note: to fancy is to think or suppose
Desperate Dan is a strongman in the British comic The Dandy

explanation.surface: Following the victory, a bloke shows off, and someone reckons he must be desperate.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to the previous clue for the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy dan is a flashy person who likes to display their skill or style.

clue.text: Wife's responsibility mostly to children

indicators.note: the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a duty is a responsibility

explanation.surface: A wife's role is chiefly the care of children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wife's' reads as Wife is. Dutch, from duchess, is Cockney slang for a wife ('my old Dutch').
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney usage a man's Dutch is his wife, from 'duchess'.

clue.text: Feel terrific — holy orders (not RC) providing a comfortable situation

indicators.note: orders as a verb arranges these letters into new order
not says the RC letters are left out of feel terrific

parts.note: taken as written, the abbreviation for Roman Catholic

explanation.surface: Feeling great after taking holy orders, though not as a Roman Catholic, makes for an easy life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'orders' rearranges FEEL TERRIFIC, less R and C ('not RC'), plus HOLY. 'holy orders' looks like one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Living the life of Riley means living in carefree luxury and ease.
